 Judgment
The petitioner has filed claim application U/Sec 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the petitioner case as follows:-
On 02.12.2023 at about 06.45 p.m, the petitioner was riding the Motor Bike bearing No.KA-40-Y-9970 (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.90/2024 proceeding on the left side of the road from Cheedachikkanahalli towards Chikkaballapur, near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Cheedachikkanahalli Village, at the same time, the John Deer Tractor bearing No.KA-40-TB-1705 and Engine No.PY3029U083732 and Chassis No.1PY5405EEPA011536, driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner, with a high speed, came from opposite direction in the same road and dashed against the petitioner's bike.

Due to which, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Jain Mission hospital, Chikkaballapura, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 02.12.2023 to 06.12.2023 and has undergone surgery and he has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/-
for surgery, medical expenses, nourishment, transportation charges and attendant charges.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 61 years and was doing Real estate business and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to move his leg and his entire body was suffered and unable to do his work and lost his source of income and he has lost his livelihood and suffered physical disability.

The accident was occurred due to (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.90/2024 rash and negligent driving of offending tractor and in this regard the Nandi Giridhama Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of offending tractor.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of offending tractor, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a and with costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.1 has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further Krishnappa V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113001707/

sentences.text: 2 denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending tractor, age, avocation and income of petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

Further admits that the tractor bearing No.KA-40-TB-1705 was covered at the material time under the policy of insurance issued by this respondent subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the alleged accident was occurred only on the part of the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.90/2024 petitioner who was riding his Motor Cycle in a careless and negligent manner and the driver of the offending tractor had no valid and effective driving licence and and there is violation of policy conditions by the respondent No.2 and the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive, and hence, pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES

01. Whether the petitioner is proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 02.12.2023 at about 6.45 p.m., near Anjaneya Swamy Temple, Cheedachikkanahalli Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of John Deer Tractor bearing registration No. KA-40-TB-1705 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?
In order to prove the case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got examined two witnesses as PW.3 and 4 and got marked 33 documents as Ex.P.1 to 33 and closed his side evidence.

The evidence of PW.2 and documents marked is to be discarded, because she left the job at Jain Mission hospital.
07.
By way of rebuttal, the respondents did not lead evidence.
Hence, the respondents evidence is taken as nil and closed its side evidence.
08. Heard both sides.

09. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:-

In affirmative  Issue No.2
In partly affirmative  Issue No.3

sentences.text: The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.1 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.90/2024 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioner that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending tractor by its driver, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 is FIR registered at Nandi Giridhama Police against driver offending tractor.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending tractor the accident took place, in which the petitioner sustained injuries.
Ex.P.3 is Police intimation.
Ex.P.4 to 6
are Sketch, Spot Mahazar and Seizer Mahazar showing the place of accident on Agalagurki - Srirampura Road, near Anjaneyaswamy Temple, Cheedachikkanahalli Village, Chikkaballapura Taluk
and after investigation the Police have seized both vehicles, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.7 is Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending tractor.

Ex.P.8 is Reply to notice which discloses that the owner of the offending tractor stating that one Punith Kumar was driving the said tractor and he had a valid driving licence and the vehicle had valid fitness certificate as on the date of accident and said offending tractor had valid insurance as on the (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.90/2024 date of accident.
Ex.P.9 and 10 are Vehicle release mahazars shows that the owner of offending tractor and petitioner executed request letter to release their vehicles which are in the custody of Police.
Ex.P.11 is IMV report shows involvement of both vehicles in the accident.

Ex.P.12 is Wound certificate shows that petitioner sustained 1) left leg proximal 1/3rd leg - visible bone deformity,
tenderness x bony crepitus present abnormal mobility present and X-ray shows fracture left both bone leg - proximal 1/3rd and 2) superficial abrasion pre patella supra posterior region and doctor opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
Ex.P.13 and 14 are the Statements of petitioner and eye-witness Manjunath.
Ex.P.15 is Photographs of two-wheeler and tractor.
Ex.P.16 is the Charge sheet shows after investigation the Investigation Officer has filed against driver of offending tractor for the offences punishable U/s 279, 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.17 is RC of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.18 is Policy of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.19 is DL of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.20 is Order sheet in CC No.2262/2023 of JMFC, Chikkaballapura, wherein the accused/driver of the offending vehicle has pleaded guilty and paid fine of (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.90/2024 Rs.2,000/-.
Ex.P.21 is Discharge summary shows petitioner fracture left both bone leg proximal 1/3rd and Ex.P.22 is OPD slips.
The petitioner got examined PW.2, but later her evidence is discarded, because she left the job at Jain Mission hospital, Chikkaballapur.

Later MRD Assistant in Jain Mission hospital,
Chikkaballapur, is examined as PW.3 and he has produced Authorization letter, Case sheet issued by Jain hospital, MLC extract and Police intimation form as per Ex.P.28 to 31.

The oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending tractor, the petitioner sustained injuries.
To disprove the case of the petitioner, the respondents have not lead evidence.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

Petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 61 years and was doing Real (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.90/2024 estate business and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and lost his source of income and became permanent disabled.
12. So far as avocation and income of the petitioner is concerned, he has not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents regarding proof of the income of the injured, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-.
13.

Looking to the nature of the injuries, it is duty of petitioner to prove his age, but petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records and SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.23 and 24 which are Aadhaar card and Driving licence.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other documents, the same can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 11.06.1960 and 11.06.1961 and the (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.90/2024 alleged accident was occurred on 02.12.2023 and there is variation in birth year.
Hence, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner as 63 years and this tribunal has assessed age of the petitioner is 63 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 61 to 65 years is '7'.
14.

sentences.text: According to the evidence of PW.4, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief-examination that the petitioner has sustained left leg both bone fracture type 1 open and he assessed physical disability for limb at 42% and to the whole body at 14% and he has produced Clinical note and X-ray as per Ex.P.32 and 33.

In his cross-examination he admits that he has treated the petitioner personally and based on the Wound certificate he has mentioned the injuries in his affidavit para 2 to 4 and at the time of Discharge petitioner condition was stable and as on today fracture is united.

In discharge summary there is (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.90/2024 advise for physiotherapy and accident taken place in the year 2022 and he has assess the disability in the year 2025 almost 3 years and that petitioner not sustained any injuries in joints and he has assessed disability for ankle and knee and the age related contributions will be there and denied to the suggestion that if any person completed at the age of 65 years they will not advise for removal of implants and admits that petitioner not suffered shortening of leg and nerve damages and that power grade is normal.
With some difficulty petitioner can do real estate work.

He was not a member of disability assessment board and admits that in their hospital there is no disability assessment board and that it is mandatory if petitioner sustained these kind of restrictions and complication, he has to take physiotherapy and denied to the suggestion that petitioner has not sustain any restriction in left lower limb and since he has not treated the petitioner, he has not a Krishnappa V vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 December, 2025

competent person to assess the disability.

However, considering the evidence of PW.4 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.90/2024 disability of the petitioner at 14%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 7 x 14/100 = Rs.1,88,160/-.
15.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:-

The petitioner has produced Discharge summary at Ex.P.21 of Jain Mission hospital,
Chikkaballapur, which shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital for 5 days.
During the aforesaid period, the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charges, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/-
under this head.

16. Pain and sufferings:- As per Ex.P.12 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.4 Doctor and as per Case sheet, Clinical note and X-ray and on account of accidental injuries, petitioner has undergone pain and agony.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
17. Loss of income during laid up period:-
As already discussed above, this tribunal has assessed (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.90/2024 the income of Rs.16,000/- per month and he was admitted in the hospital for 5 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast two months.
Thus, taking into account the income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 2) under this head.
18. Medical Expenses:- The petitioner has got marked entire medical bills and advance bills as per Ex.P.25 and 26 for Rs.1,25,722/-.
To disprove the said bill, the respondent No.1 has not produced any documents nor any evidence.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,25,722/- under this head.

19. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.

20. Future medical expenses:- According to doctor PW.4, the petitioner needs one more surgery in the form of implant removal, for which approximate (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.90/2024 cost of Rs.50,000/- is required, but he not produced any estimation regarding future medical expenses.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/-

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl. Head of compensation Amount in No. Rs.
1. Loss of future income 1,88,160-00 2.
Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00 3. Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and conveyance  charges 4.
Medical Expenses 1,25,722-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 32,000-00  period 7.
Future medical expenses 30,000-00  Total 4,65,882-00 22.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,65,882/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.90/2024 medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

23. Regarding liability:- On service of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and respondent No.1 has filed objections and contest the matter, but despite sufficient opportunity, they have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove their contention.
On the date of accident policy was in force.
Hence, respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay above said compensation amount.
Respondent No.1 Insurance Company is directed to deposit above said compensation amount within two months from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:-

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,65,882/- (Rupees Four lakhs sixty five thousand eight hundred and eighty two only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
